newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: CREDITANSTALT TENDER DECISION SEEN IN HOURS - RADIO.
newsitem.headline: CREDITANSTALT TENDER DECISION SEEN IN HOURS - RADIO.

text.p: Austrian Finance Minister Viktor Klima will decide in the next few hours whether to reopen a tender for Creditanstalt-Bankverein to allow bidders to improve their offers, Austrian radio said on Friday.
No one at the finance ministry was immediately available for comment. Earlier a spokesman said it was unclear whether there would be an announcement before the weekend.
Bidders for the state's 70 percent of Creditanstalt ordinary shares said they too were waiting for official word from the government.
Market leader Bank Austria is up against rival offers from a consortium led by insurer EA-Generali and entrepreneur Karl Wlaschek, an outsider.
Bank Austria has topped the bidding, putting up some 16 billion schillings for the state's stake that is worth around 14.3 billion schillings at current market prices.

Klima, a Social Democrat, has come under pressure from conservatives within the government to reject Bank Austria's bid on the grounds it would not be a genuine privatisation. The Social Democrat-run City of Vienna effectively controls Bank Austria.
Preferred shares in Creditanstalt firmed 5.81 percent in Vienna on brisk turnover ahead of the finance ministry decision on whether to reopen the tender.
At 1236 GMT Creditanstalt preferred were 27 schillings up at 491.50 on turnover of 57,962 lots, making the stock the ATX index's biggest gainer and second most actively traded share.
Some dealers traced the rise to investor interest from abroad but most said market makers were behind the move.
"Institutional investors don't want to touch Creditanstalt with a barge pole at the moment," a trader said. -- Vienna Newsroom, 43-1-53112-258
